notes: Check batch at 551e3ab with the uncommitted Readability rewrite: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier, and each result.json records skill_hash 7945a793..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder; every transcript contains the new rule text ("A line break is not decomposition" and the heading "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance"). Haiku-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md, the other three SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal: totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day) and empty results for [] are correct in all four. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status, a bad date and a non-string amount; haiku-1 raises FunctionClauseError for a missing key and a non-string amount and accepts an unknown status, recorded under other_violations.

Rules changed since d04061d and graded against the current text: the with rule, the do: rule, the pipeline rule, the captures rule, the Enum/Map table (two new rows, neither shape present), the renamed `->` rule and the two new rules. The with rule is decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`" (build/1 in all four, whose body {:ok, summarize(...)} cannot fail; under the d04061d text this single call had to be a case, as all five runs of 2026-10-23 wrote it) and by "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result, the recursive `parse_rows(rest, [order | orders])` of a hand-written loop, is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays" (sonnet-1 lines 79-81, sonnet-2 lines 75-77). The do: rule's new text adds no violation: no run has a one-line if, a for, a fn or a call-carrying capture in a do: body, and the mixed functions (sonnet-1 parse_orders/2; sonnet-2 parse_orders/2, parse_order/1, parse_amount/1, parse_placed_at/1) set block clauses apart with blank lines, "A function may mix the forms ... each block clause set apart with a blank line". The pipeline rule's new "A pipeline never sits on one line" finds no one-line pipeline in any run. The captures rule's new paragraph decides three violations: "A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn: the body goes on the line after the `->`, and `end` closes it on a line of its own" (haiku-2 line 87, sonnet-1 line 172, sonnet-2 line 164); under the d04061d text the same sort_by fn was held clean (2026-10-23 opus-1 line 228). Unchanged rules (atoms, lists, dates, money, Naming, processes) are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard: haiku-1 keeps the status a string, so the atoms rule is not exercised there; haiku-1 and haiku-2 prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order.

One expression per line, and tabular clauses (new, clean in all four). Constructs: the parse_status/1 do: tables (haiku-2 146-149, sonnet-1 140-143, sonnet-2 132-135), decided by "Parallel clauses may stay compact ... when they form a table: each row is one alternative of the same decision or mapping ... and at most one final row catches what did not match and reports it"; the one-line do: heads (haiku-2 91; sonnet-1 74, 76, 176; sonnet-2 70, 72, 103, 118, 130) and the one-line -> clauses of haiku-1 (40-41, 69-71, 77-78) and haiku-2 (96-97, 125-127, 133-135, 141-142), each a selection and one tuple, call or comparison, decided by "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces"; the long single-line bodies {:ok, %{customers: summarize_customers(orders), top_customers: top_customers(orders)}} (sonnet-1 70, sonnet-2 66) and {currency, Enum.reduce(..., &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2))} (haiku-1 108, sonnet-2 156), decided by "Count expressions, not calls or brackets". The one-line sort_by fns are left to the captures and `->` rules under "the rules below apply it construct by construct, where each construct's own syntax adds conditions of its own": the line holds a fn pattern and one tuple, which this rule alone allows.

Name a step instead of wrapping an expression (new, clean in all four). Constructs: the bindings latest (all four), order (haiku-1 55, haiku-2 111) and total (haiku-2 67-72), each used once, decided by "A binding earns its place when it names a recognizable thing or a stage of the computation ... or makes the expression around it substantially clearer" (the latest order, the built order, the per-currency sum lifted out of a tuple), so none "only renames a value used once"; the sonnet runs' formatter-wrapped {:ok, %Order{...}} (sonnet-1 93-100, sonnet-2 92-99), held clean because it is a tag around a struct literal laid out one field per line, with no distinct computational steps inside it to name ("what helps is finding the distinct conceptual steps inside it and giving one a name, when the name says something"); this is the one judgment call under this rule, and haiku-1 and haiku-2 bind the same value as order first. No run wraps a nested computation.

Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line (renamed and rewritten; the 2026-10-23 order-report grades did not list it; violated in haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2). The three violations are the one-line sort_by fn, decided by "A `fn` passed as an argument follows the capture rule: when it binds names, its body goes on the line after the `->`." Clean constructs: the reduce_while case of haiku-1 (40-41) and haiku-2 (96-97), {:ok, order} -> {:cont, ...} above {:error, _reason} = error -> {:halt, error}, read as a table with one final report row ("Parallel clauses may stay compact ... at most one final row catches what did not match and reports it, in whatever shape the report needs"), not as clauses doing different kinds of work, since both bodies are tagged values for reduce_while and neither does the continuing work itself; haiku-1's parse_amount/1 (69-71) and parse_placed_at/1 (77-78) and haiku-2's string_field/2 (125-127), parse_amount/1 (133-135) and parse_datetime/1 (141-142), which have two error rows and so are not strictly tables, held clean by "or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern", every clause under 70 characters after the indentation (longest 60, haiku-2 line 142); the sonnet runs' cases, every body on its own line with blank lines between clauses, as "when one clause breaks, every clause of that `case` does" requires. Under the d04061d `->` rule ("pattern and body are each one plain term") haiku-1 69-71 and haiku-2 125-127 would have been read differently; the current text allows them.

Other rules: haiku-1 and haiku-2 give build/1 a @doc without ## Examples (the documentation rule, as in earlier sweeps); haiku-1 matches the required keys in a single-clause parse_order/1 head with no catch-all and never validates the status (Parse external data into structs where it enters the system, same wording as the 2026-10-21-check grade). Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have doctests, structs with @enforce_keys and @type t, and no case or with nested inside another; no other violation was found.
